sentences.text: Shri Surendra Kumar Gupta - Ga for State.
Heard on IA No.21669/2021, which is the first application under Section 389 of Cr.P.C. for suspension of jail sentence moved on behalf of sole appellant - Bankatlal @ Banti

The appellant has been convicted under Section 363, 366, 342, 376 (D) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for two years with fine of Rs.1000/-, three years RI with fine of Rs.1000/-, three months RI and 20 years RI with a fine of Rs.5000/- with default stipulation.

As per the case on prosecution on 13.04.2018, the complainant Rafiq lodged a missing report of her niece at outpost Daloda to the effect that her niece had gone to her maternal aunt's home 4-5 days back and had gone missing since 11.04.2018.
On this report, a crime at Crime No. 134/2018 Under Section 363 of the IPC.
On 08.05.2018, the police recovered the victim from the custody of the appellant and the co-accused Radheshyam.

The police launched an investigation, and during the course of the same, it came to the revelation that the appellant, on the pretext of marriage, took away the victim by enticing her and inducing her.

It is further the case of the prosecution that the appellant and co-accused had taken the victim towards Pratapgarh and kept her in a hut for five days, whereas the appellant 2 CRA-4682-2021 committed rape over the victim by threatening her.
Thereafter, the victim was taken to Gujarat and again she was subjected to rape.
The police arrested the appellant and co-accused and after completion of the investigation, submitted the charge sheet.
The appellant was put on to trial and the Ld.
Trial court by impugned judgment found the appellant guilty of offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 342, 376(d), 376(2)n of IPC and under Section 5L/6 of Pocso Act and convicted him as above.
Counsel for appellant argued that the prosecutrix had stayed with the appellant for about 25 days.
She travelled to different States of Rajasthan and Gujarat.
The missing report was lodged after two days, and she was recovered after 25 days.
According to he prosecution, her age is 16 and half years and no source has been provided by the prosecution for recording the age of the prosecutrix in the scholar register.
Counsel for appellant argued that there is no allegation of rape against the said appellant.

sentences.text: Counsel for the State opposed the prayer and submitted that the age of the accused persons is more than 30 years, and the prosecutrix was a minor, and, therefore, no case is made out for suspension of jail sentence.

After hearing learned counsel for parties and considering the statement of the prosecutrix, we find that the prosecutrix had travelled along with the appellant to different States and stayed for 25 days.
There was no resistance alarm raised by the prosecutrix.
She appears to be a consenting party.
Apart from that, the prosecutrix has failed to prove the source on the basis of which the date of birth was recorded in the scholar register.
The appellant has already undergone an actual jail sentence of seven and half years.
The appeal 3 CRA-4682-2021 is of the year 2021 and the final hearing of the appeal may take time, therefore, we are of the view that the present application deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, the application is allowed.

The jail sentence of appellant - Bankatlal @ Banti is suspended upon his depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees fifty thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 18/11/2025 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Registry.
With the aforesaid, I.A is allowed and disposed of.
CC as per rules.
(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) (PREM NARAY  JUDGE JUDG
